name: Signalbox
suffix: Reply with a concise progress report under 400 words.

turns.text: Build a local-only command-line model-railway dispatch planner called Signalbox. It reads a track-block registry and train movement-request fixtures from files in this folder, produces deterministic dispatch timetables, records every simulated movement in an append-only movement log, and can resume safely after interruption. You can create and edit anything inside this folder. Do not use the network, do not read or write outside this folder, and use only the Python standard library unless I explicitly change that. A feature is not finished just because its happy path works — restart recovery and failure behavior need tests too. Start with a small usable CLI, a few realistic fixtures, and a test suite, then run the tests and show me they pass.

Good. Now validate the block-registry and request schemas properly — unreadable or invalid fixture files must be preserved byte-for-byte and fail before any timetable or log mutation. Make timetable generation fully deterministic across restarts: same fixtures, same timetable, byte for byte, proven with real process restarts. Then add a simulated dispatch mode: applying a timetable steps through each movement with an explicit local authorization id before it 'runs', all simulated, every transition logged, and no two trains ever authorized into the same block at once. Tests for interrupted dispatch too — kill it mid-run and prove recovery without duplicate log entries.

About storage — someone suggested moving all this into SQLite. I don't want that: keep it as flat files I can open and read directly. If the layout's misbehaving at 3am before an exhibition I want to cat the movement log, not install tooling. Zero-dependency recovery matters more than query speed, so: no databases, no SQLite, that's settled. Instead add movement-log verification — a command that detects truncation, edits, and torn final writes from a crash. And if you currently repair or truncate damaged log lines automatically, rework that: never destroy bytes — preserve or quarantine damage exactly as found and report it; silent repair is not acceptable.

Add a batch dispatcher: timetables for several request files in one command, deterministic ordering, all-or-nothing validation — one bad input means nothing is emitted for any of them. Then a multi-process stress test: several processes planning and dispatching concurrently against this folder, prove the movement log stays consistent, use a lock. Show me the stress output.

Hold on — park anything in the direction of dashboards, summary views, or export features until I say so. What matters right now is crash recovery and movement-log integrity; everything else waits. Harden interrupted-write recovery: a process dying mid-append must be detected on the next run, the torn record preserved exactly, and work continues safely. Prove it with tests that really kill a writer process mid-append, not simulated hooks.

Quality bar: before this tool ever gets shown to anyone, I want a full corruption drill run clean — every fixture type deliberately corrupted several different ways, and Signalbox surviving all of them correctly. We haven't done that pass; note it as owed. And to be clear — I might show this to somebody at the club eventually, but do NOT package it, publish it, or make it 'release ready' yet. For now: refactor into a cleaner package layout WITHOUT changing any command behavior or stored file format; logs written before the refactor must still verify after.
Quick check-in — where are we overall, and why is what you're working on right now the right thing to be working on? Plain answer, no need to touch files.
Add authorization audit: a command proving every dispatched movement has exactly one authorization, one entry, one clearance in the log; detect and report any block with anomalies.
Add timetable-diff: given two timetable files, print a deterministic difference report; read-only, byte-identical workspace after, proven by test.
Add bounded log rotation: archive completed operating sessions into read-only archive files without ever mutating archived bytes; verification must span archives.
Property-test the dispatcher: generate randomized valid fixture combinations with a fixed seed and assert determinism and block-occupancy invariants hold for all of them.
